extra.message: The `packet_ref` parameter from `request.GET.get('packet_ref')` is directly concatenated into a file path (`BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref`) without sanitization. An attacker with a valid internal token can use `../` sequences to read arbitrary files on the server.

The `relay_ref` parameter from `request.GET.get('url')` is passed directly to `urllib.request.urlopen()` without any URL validation. An attacker with a valid internal token can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other internal resources.

User-controlled input from `request.GET.get('fragment')` is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to Remote Code Execution.

User-controlled input from `request.GET.get('host')` is directly concatenated into a shell command passed to `os.system()`. An attacker with a valid internal token can inject arbitrary shell commands using metacharacters like `;`, `|`, `&&`, etc.

The XML parser is configured with `load_dtd=True`, `resolve_entities=True`, and `no_network=False`, which enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks. An attacker can craft XML payloads that read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service.

The `ref` parameter from `request.GET.get('ref')` is used to construct a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem. Additionally, sensitive data (SSN, credit card) from query parameters is written to the file.

The `name` parameter from `request.GET.get('name')` is used to construct a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences to write arbitrary content to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

The `acct_identity_ping_333` endpoint does not call `_wrk_gate(request)` to verify the internal operations token, unlike all other endpoints in this module. Any unauthenticated user can access this endpoint.

User-controlled input from `request.GET.get('fragment')` is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions to execute arbitrary Python code.

The `name` parameter from `request.GET.get('name')` is used to construct a file path for writing arbitrary request body content. An attacker can use `../` sequences to write files with arbitrary content to any location on the filesystem.

The XML parser is configured with `load_dtd=True`, `resolve_entities=True`, and `no_network=False`, which enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks. User-supplied XML from `request.body` is parsed with this insecure configuration.
The `acct_vault_stash_233` function writes sensitive PII (SSN and credit card numbers) to a JSON file on disk in plaintext without any encryption.
The `acct_xml_fold_451` function parses untrusted XML input with dangerous parser settings that enable entity resolution and DTD loading, which is a form of insecure deserialization of XML data.

User-controlled input from the `fragment` query parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), enabling arbitrary code execution on the server.

User-controlled input from the `fragment` query parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This allows both Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and reflected XSS. An attacker can inject arbitrary Jinja2 template expressions or HTML/JavaScript via the `fragment` parameter. The rendered output is returned with `content_type='text/html'`, making XSS directly exploitable.

The route 'ops/folio/acct-roster-card-001/' maps to partner_console.acct_roster_card_001. Based on the naming pattern ('acct-roster-card'), this endpoint likely exposes account data. It is registered at the top-level URL configuration without any authentication middleware or decorator visible, making it accessible to unauthenticated users.
The route 'ops/after/acct-lane-149/' maps to partner_console.acct_return_lane_149. This endpoint is registered without authentication protection.
The route 'ops/identity/acct-hint-359/' maps to partner_console.acct_identity_hint_359. This endpoint provides identity hints and is registered without authentication protection.
The route 'ops/nonce/acct-roll-409/' maps to partner_console.acct_nonce_roll_409. This endpoint deals with nonce/security token rolling and is registered without authentication protection.

The `safe_break` template filter uses `mark_safe()` on user-provided content without first HTML-escaping it. When this filter is applied to user-controlled data (such as contact names, notes, escalation comments, or organization notes), any embedded HTML or JavaScript will be rendered and executed in the browser. For example, if a user enters `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` in a comment field, and that field is rendered in a template using `{{ comment|safe_break }}`, the script will execute.

The acct_vendor_ping_003 function accepts a user-controlled URL parameter and passes it directly to urllib.request.urlopen without any validation. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery attacks where an attacker can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, potentially accessing internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or performing port scanning.

The acct_shell_probe_399 function accepts a user-controlled 'host' parameter and directly concatenates it into a shell command string passed to os.system(). This allows command injection where an attacker can execute arbitrary system commands by injecting shell metacharacters.

The acct_jinja_cast_381 function takes user input from the 'fragment' parameter and passes it directly to Jinja2's Template.render() method. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) attacks where an attacker can execute arbitrary Python code within the template context.

The acct_xml_fold_451 function parses XML with lxml's XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables XXE attacks where an attacker can inject external entities to read local files, make network requests, or cause denial of service.

The 'packet_ref' parameter from request.GET is used directly in path construction via 'BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref'. An attacker can traverse directories using '../' sequences to read arbitrary files from the filesystem.

The 'ref' parameter is user-controlled and inserted into a file path via f-string: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json". Path traversal sequences like '../../../etc/cron.d/malicious' allow writing files outside the intended directory.

The endpoint /ops/xml/acct-fold-451/ maps to partner_console.acct_xml_fold_451 without any visible authentication wrapper. The endpoint name suggests XML processing functionality which could be vulnerable to XXE attacks.

The SECRET_KEY setting uses a hardcoded fallback value 'dev-secret-change-me-please-not-for-production' that will be used if the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. In production, this weak hardcoded secret enables session forgery, password reset token forgery, and cryptographic signature bypass attacks.

The AppLoginView login handler does not implement rate limiting. While LoginEvent.recent_failures() exists in the model, it is never called or checked in the login view to block or throttle repeated login attempts. An attacker can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing attacks.

In the invite_accept view, after authenticating a user (line 143) and calling login(request, user) (line 145), the session is not explicitly regenerated. While Django's login() does call session.cycle_key() internally, the broader concern is that this is a public endpoint (no @login_required) that creates accounts and logs users in. The session from the anonymous browsing phase is carried through account creation without explicit regeneration before the authenticate/login call.

The endpoint reflects the `Origin` header value directly into the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header and sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint.
The endpoint creates an unverified SSL context using `ssl._create_unverified_context()`, which disables certificate verification. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The `acct_workset_rebind_191` function takes the entire user-supplied JSON payload and uses `dict.update()` to overwrite a workset dictionary that includes security-sensitive fields like `role`, `tier`, and `approved`.

The `acct_nonce_roll_409` function uses Python's `random` module (which is not cryptographically secure) to generate nonce/code values. The `random` module uses a Mersenne Twister PRNG which is predictable.
The `acct_digest_fold_273` function uses MD5 to hash a user-supplied phrase. MD5 is cryptographically broken and should not be used for any security-sensitive hashing.

The `acct_vault_stash_233` function accepts SSN and credit card numbers via GET query parameters (`request.GET.get('ssn')`, `request.GET.get('card')`). Query parameters are logged in web server access logs, browser history, and proxy logs.

The `acct_badge_gate_439` function makes access control decisions based on the `ops_badge` cookie value. Since cookies are client-controlled, any attacker can set `ops_badge=lead` to gain elevated access.
The `acct_nonce_roll_409` function uses Python's `random` module (which is not cryptographically secure) to generate nonce/code values. The `random` module uses a predictable PRNG.
The `acct_vault_stash_233` function accepts SSN and credit card numbers via GET query parameters. These values will be logged in web server access logs, browser history, and potentially proxy logs.
The database password has a hardcoded default value 'crm_saas' that will be used if the DB_PASSWORD environment variable is not set. This is a cleartext credential stored in source code.

The file contains a hardcoded password 'Demo!Password123' stored in the DEMO_PASSWORD constant. This password is used to create demo user accounts across multiple roles including platform admin, account managers, support agents, and customer contacts. If this management command is accidentally run in a production environment, it would create accounts with a publicly known password that attackers could use to gain unauthorized access.

The acct_return_lane_149 function accepts a user-controlled 'lane' parameter from either GET or POST and passes it directly to Django's redirect() function without validation. This allows an attacker to construct URLs that redirect users to malicious external sites, facilitating phishing attacks.

The acct_origin_mirror_369 function reflects the Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to 'true'. This is a dangerous CORS configuration that allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests to the API.

The acct_trust_drift_429 function creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context(), which disables certificate verification. It then makes an HTTPS request without validating the server's certificate, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The acct_vault_stash_233 function writes sensitive data including SSN and credit card numbers to a JSON file without encryption. It accepts these values from GET parameters which may be logged in server logs, proxy logs, and browser history. The data is stored in plaintext on the filesystem.

The create_key view passes the full ApiKey model object to the template. While the secret itself is passed separately as revealed_secret, the ApiKey object may contain sensitive metadata or the key_hash which could facilitate attacks.

The acct_trust_drift_429 function uses ssl._create_unverified_context() to create an SSL context with certificate verification disabled, then uses this context with urllib.request.urlopen() to make an HTTPS request. This disables protection against man-in-the-middle attacks.

URL pattern 'ops/shell/acct-probe-399/' maps to partner_console.acct_shell_probe_399. The endpoint name 'shell_probe' strongly suggests it executes shell commands. If user-controlled input reaches this function and is passed to shell execution functions (subprocess, os.system, etc.) without proper sanitization, it would allow arbitrary command execution on the server.

URL pattern 'ops/jinja/acct-cast-381/' maps to partner_console.acct_jinja_cast_381. The endpoint name 'jinja_cast' suggests it renders Jinja2 templates. If this endpoint accepts user-controlled template strings and renders them without sandboxing, it would be vulnerable to Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI).

URL pattern 'ops/xml/acct-fold-451/' maps to partner_console.acct_xml_fold_451. The name 'xml_fold' suggests XML document processing. If this endpoint parses user-controlled XML without disabling external entities, it would be vulnerable to XXE attacks.

The DEBUG setting defaults to True if the DJANGO_DEBUG environment variable is not set. Debug mode exposes sensitive information including full stack traces, environment variables, and configuration details in error pages.

Default database username and password are hardcoded as 'crm_saas'. If these credentials are not overridden by environment variables and the database is accessible, attackers can connect using these known credentials.

The custom 'safe_break' template filter is applied to escalation.customer_summary field. If this filter converts newlines to HTML breaks and marks the result as safe without sanitizing other HTML content, it allows stored XSS attacks through the escalation summary field.

The custom 'safe_break' template filter is applied to comment body (c.body). If this filter marks content as safe without proper HTML sanitization, attackers can inject JavaScript through comment submissions.
The custom 'safe_break' filter is used on escalation.customer_summary field. Without proper HTML sanitization in the filter, this enables stored XSS through the customer-visible summary field.
The custom 'safe_break' filter is applied to escalation.internal_summary (staff-only notes). If the filter doesn't sanitize HTML, this allows stored XSS through internal notes.
The custom 'safe_break' filter is used on comment body content in the escalation comment thread. Without HTML sanitization, this enables stored XSS.
The custom 'safe_break' filter is applied to org.notes field. If the filter renders content as safe HTML without sanitization, attackers can inject JavaScript through organization notes.
The custom 'safe_break' filter is used on deal.notes field. Without proper HTML sanitization, this allows stored XSS through deal notes.

The password reset endpoint uses Django's built-in PasswordResetView without any rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited password reset emails, potentially causing email flooding or user enumeration.

The invite_accept view handles account creation and password setting without any rate limiting. While the token provides some protection, an attacker with a valid token could attempt brute-force form submissions.

The safe_break template filter uses mark_safe() to render user-provided text with newlines converted to
tags. If the input value contains user-controlled content (e.g., notes, comments, summaries), HTML/JavaScript in the value will be rendered unescaped, leading to stored XSS.

The _seed_users method creates staff users (platform admin, account managers, support agents) with the hardcoded DEMO_PASSWORD via make_password(DEMO_PASSWORD). These are privileged accounts with the same known password.
The _seed_portal_user_for_first_invite method creates customer contact portal users with the same hardcoded DEMO_PASSWORD. These accounts have access to customer-facing portal features.

The navigation context processor passes the full User object as 'nav_user' to every template context. The User model contains sensitive fields including password hash (from AbstractBaseUser), last_login_ip, and potentially other sensitive attributes. This data crosses a trust boundary from server to rendered output.

The invite_accept view passes the full ContactInvite object (including the token and related contact/organization objects) to the template context. The invite object contains the secret token and related user data.

The webhook URL validation in clean_target_url attempts to block SSRF by checking for private/loopback IPs, but the validation is incomplete and can be bypassed. It does not block: (1) IPv6 private addresses beyond ::1 (e.g., [::ffff:127.0.0.1], [fc00::], [fe80::]), (2) DNS rebinding attacks where a hostname resolves to a private IP at request time, (3) URL redirects that lead to internal services, (4) decimal/octal/hex IP representations (e.g., 0x7f000001, 2130706433), (5) cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254 is only partially blocked via startswith('169.254.')).

The `write_audit` function writes audit events to the database with user-influenced data in the `action`, `summary`, `target_repr`, and `metadata` fields without sanitization. While the `action` parameter is typically set by application code, the `summary` field often includes user-controlled data (e.g., email addresses, organization names). An attacker who controls these values could inject misleading audit entries to cover their tracks or frame other users.

The `get_client_ip` function trusts the first entry in the `X-Forwarded-For` header without validation. This header is easily spoofable by clients unless stripped by a trusted reverse proxy. The spoofed IP is used for audit logging (LoginEvent, AuditEvent) and stored on the User model (last_login_ip), which could allow attackers to forge their apparent IP address in audit trails.

The `AdminUserForm` ModelForm exposes the `role`, `is_active`, and `is_staff` fields for editing. While the form is named 'Admin-only', if the view using this form doesn't properly restrict access to only platform admins, any staff user with access could escalate their own or others' roles to `platform_admin` or grant `is_staff` access to the Django admin panel.

The invite acceptance flow checks if `invite.contact.user` is None before creating a new user, but this check and the subsequent user creation are not atomic. If two requests with the same invite token are processed concurrently, both could pass the `user is None` check and attempt to create duplicate users with the same email, or one could overwrite the other's password.

The `acct_digest_fold_273` endpoint uses MD5 hashing, which is cryptographically broken. If this is used for any security-sensitive purpose (password hashing, integrity verification), it is vulnerable to collision and preimage attacks.
Hardcoded verification PINs/credentials are stored in the source code: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. These are used as authentication verifiers for the identity hint endpoint.
A default SSN value '111-22-3333' and credit card number '4111111111111111' are hardcoded as default parameter values in the acct_vault_stash_233 function.
The 'lane' parameter from user input is directly passed to Django's redirect() function without validation. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to a malicious external site.
The acct_digest_fold_273 function uses MD5 for hashing, which is cryptographically broken. While the exact use case is unclear, MD5 should not be used for any security-sensitive hashing.
The acct_vault_stash_233 function returns the full filesystem path of the stored file in the JSON response. This leaks internal server directory structure.
The acct_dock_shelf_388 function returns the full filesystem path of the stored file in the JSON response, leaking internal server directory structure.
The acct_identity_hint_359 function returns different error messages and HTTP status codes for 'unknown handle' (404) vs 'bad verifier' (403). This allows an attacker to enumerate valid handles.

The acct_workset_rebind_191 function blindly updates a workset dictionary with all user-supplied JSON payload fields using workset.update(payload). An attacker can override any field including 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance'.

When `ENABLE_REAL_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` is True, the `test_delivery` function sends HTTP requests to the webhook's `target_url` using `urllib.request.urlopen()`. While the WebhookForm validates URLs at creation time, the URL validation at form submission time may be bypassed via DNS rebinding (DNS resolves to public IP during validation but to internal IP at request time).

The `acct_delta_121` function allows user-controlled input to set the `state` field of a ledger object. An attacker can set the state to any arbitrary value (e.g., 'approved') regardless of business logic.
The `acct_frame_slip_419` function explicitly disables XSS protection (`X-XSS-Protection: 0`) and sets an empty Content-Security-Policy header, removing browser-side security protections.
The `acct_frame_slip_419` function explicitly disables XSS protection (`X-XSS-Protection: 0`) and sets an empty Content-Security-Policy header, removing browser-side protections.

The `acct_return_lane_149` function takes a `lane` parameter from user input (GET or POST) and passes it directly to Django's `redirect()` function. This allows an attacker to craft a URL that redirects users to an arbitrary external site, which can be used for phishing attacks. While this endpoint requires an internal token, the redirect itself could be used in social engineering.

The PostgreSQL database connection configuration does not include any SSL/TLS parameters (such as sslmode, OPTIONS with sslmode=require, etc.). Database traffic including credentials and query data is transmitted in cleartext.

The get_client_ip function extracts the client IP from the HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header without any validation or whitelist of trusted proxies. Attackers can spoof arbitrary IP addresses by setting this header, which will be recorded in audit logs (LoginEvent, AuditEvent) and could bypass any IP-based access controls or rate limiting.

The CSVImportForm.organization field uses an unscoped queryset (Organization.objects.all()) that exposes all organization IDs and names in the form's HTML select options. If this form is rendered to users with limited organization access, they can see the complete list of all organizations in the system, including those they should not have visibility into.

The OrganizationForm initializes owner and assigned_staff fields with unscoped querysets that expose all users with staff roles (User.objects.filter(role__in=[...])). The form accepts a requesting_user parameter but only uses it to determine plan change permissions, not to scope the user querysets. This exposes all staff member details (IDs, names, emails) to anyone who can view this form, potentially including customer contacts.

The navigation context processor returns the full User model object as 'nav_user' in the template context. The User model contains sensitive fields including the password hash (even if hashed, this should not cross trust boundaries), last_login_ip (personally identifiable information), is_staff, is_superuser status flags, and other internal fields. Passing complete model objects to templates violates the principle of least privilege and exposes sensitive data to the presentation layer where it could be accidentally rendered or accessed.

The invite_accept view calls write_audit with user-controlled email address embedded in the summary string (f"Customer contact {user.email} activated their account"). If the email contains special characters or newlines, it can inject forged log entries into the audit trail.

The Webhook model stores the signing secret in plaintext (CharField) in the database. If the database is compromised, attackers can extract these secrets and forge webhook requests to the configured endpoints.

The acct_nonce_roll_409 function uses Python's random module to generate security-sensitive tokens/codes. The random module is not cryptographically secure and uses a deterministic algorithm that can be predicted if enough output is observed.

The user_list view passes a paginated queryset of full User model objects to the template via the 'page' context variable. User objects typically contain password hashes, API tokens, authentication credentials, and other sensitive fields that should not be exposed to the template layer.

The user_edit view passes the full target User model object to the template as 'target_user'. This object contains the user's password hash, API tokens, and other sensitive authentication credentials.

The index view passes recent_audit (AuditEvent queryset with select_related('actor')) to the template. AuditEvent objects reference User objects as 'actor' which contain sensitive fields like password hashes.
The create_contact view passes the full Organization model object to the template. Organization objects may contain sensitive business data, internal notes, or configuration details.
The edit_contact view passes the full Organization model object to the template via the 'org' variable.
The home view passes full Organization model objects and escalation querysets to the customer-facing portal template. Organization objects may contain internal-only fields.
The dashboard view constructs a context containing Organization, Deal, Escalation, AuditEvent, and Notification model objects. All are passed as full ORM objects to the template.
The list_deals view passes a paginated queryset of full Deal model objects to the template via 'page' context variable.
The detail_deal view passes the full Deal model object to the template.
The metadata view passes the full Document model object to the template.
The detail view passes full Escalation and EscalationComment model objects to the template.
The detail_org view passes the Organization object along with related Contact, Deal, Escalation, Document, ApiKey, Webhook, and AuditEvent querysets to the template. All are full model objects.
The list_notifications view passes full Notification model objects to the template.
The list_hooks view passes Webhook and WebhookDelivery model objects to the template. Webhook objects contain secret keys.

The test_delivery function in webhooks.py makes HTTP requests to user-controlled URLs when ENABLE_REAL_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY is True. While the WebhookForm likely validates URLs, the validation happens at form submission time (create/edit), but the URL stored in the database could be manipulated or the validation could be bypassed.

Nineteen operational endpoints from partner_console (paths including /ops/shell/acct-probe-399/, /ops/jinja/acct-cast-381/, /ops/xml/acct-fold-451/, etc.) are mounted unconditionally on the URL configuration without visible authentication or IP restrictions in the routing layer. These endpoint names suggest sensitive diagnostic/administrative functions (shell, jinja, xml processing).

Organization website URL is rendered directly in an href attribute without protocol validation. Django's autoescaping does not prevent javascript: protocol attacks. If an organization sets their website to 'javascript:alert(document.cookie)', clicking the link would execute arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser.

Organization website URL is rendered directly in an href attribute without protocol validation. If an organization sets their website to a javascript: URL, clicking the link would execute arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser context.
The field.help_text is rendered using |safe filter. If help_text contains user-controlled data (e.g., dynamically generated from user input), this creates an XSS vulnerability.
The field.help_text is rendered using |safe filter. If help_text derives from user-controlled data, this creates XSS.

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is only set to True in the `if not DEBUG` block (line 125). When DEBUG is True (which is the default), session cookies lack the Secure flag and can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. Since DEBUG defaults to True, this is the default state.

The AppLoginView creates LoginEvent records with user-controlled HTTP_USER_AGENT data (truncated to 300 chars) without sanitization. While the user agent is typically set by browsers, it can be manipulated by attackers to inject control characters or newline sequences into audit logs.
The acct_frame_slip_419 function explicitly disables security headers (X-XSS-Protection and Content-Security-Policy), weakening the application's security posture.

MEDIA_ROOT is constructed using an environment variable (MEDIA_ROOT) without validation or sanitization. If an attacker can influence this environment variable, they could control where uploaded files are stored on the filesystem, potentially allowing writes to arbitrary locations outside the intended media directory.

Form help_text is rendered with the |safe filter. While help_text is typically developer-controlled, if any form subclass dynamically sets help_text based on user input, this would render unsanitized HTML.

SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE is set to False, meaning session cookies persist after the user closes their browser. Combined with SESSION_COOKIE_AGE of 8 hours, sessions remain valid on disk even after browser closure.
